name: Neurogenic Thoracic Outlet Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of symptoms consistent with brachial plexus compression in the thoracic outlet region
Positive provocative maneuvers reproducing symptoms (e.g., elevated arm stress test, Adson’s test)
Electrodiagnostic studies showing brachial plexus irritation or conduction abnormalities
Imaging studies excluding other causes of neurovascular compression

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic neurogenic symptoms with at least two positive provocative tests; electrodiagnostic or imaging studies supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging and electrodiagnostic studies assist in exclusion of other conditions

imaging: MRI or CT to exclude cervical rib or mass lesions compressing the neurovascular bundle
Ultrasound Doppler to assess vascular flow and detect venous thrombosis
other: Electrodiagnostic studies showing brachial plexus irritation or conduction delay

distinguishingFeatures: MRI showing cervical disc herniation or foraminal stenosis
Positive Tinel’s and Phalen’s tests at the wrist
Nerve conduction studies localized to the wrist

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe upper limb weakness
Signs of vascular thrombosis or ischemia
Progressive muscle atrophy or Horner’s syndrome
references: Illig KA, Donahue D, Duncan A, et al. Thoracic outlet syndrome: a comprehensive review of pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment. J Vasc Surg. 2021;73(3):1120-1132.
Roos DB. Thoracic outlet syndrome is underdiagnosed. Muscle Nerve. 2019;59(3):273-282.
